# RustyNES v2.9.5 — "Caliper"

The accuracy release of the line to v3.0.0. Every open item in the accuracy ledger and the line plan now has an outcome and the evidence for it:

- **fixed**: a test failed first, and reverting the fix fails it again;
- **closed**: refuted, or settled by documentation;
- **moved**: to the release where it belongs.

**Four emulation fixes land.** One of them changes the save-state format, so **`.rns` save states from v2.9.4 or earlier do not load** in this release. They fail with a version error; they are never misread.

## What changed in emulation

- **The frame counter no longer clocks twice for one pulse.** A `$4017` write in 5-step mode clocks the length counters when it takes effect. If that lands one CPU cycle after the sequencer's own clock, hardware gives one clock and this core gave two. Hardware emits these clocks on APU-cycle boundaries, and both land in the same one. The rule comes from blargg's ten `apu_test` ROMs, which pin the boundary to the cycle in both sequencer modes. Four of them had failed since v2.6.2, when they were first read, and all ten are now gated.
- **Scanline 0 on a composite PPU.** When an odd frame skips the last dot of the pre-render line, sprites on scanline 0 draw their first pixel at X=0 (the NESdev thread that AccuracyCoin cites explains why). AccuracyCoin's `Sprites On Scanline 0` now identifies this core as a composite 2C02. It used to report an RGB PPU, because the two frames it compares never differed.
- **OAM DMA fills the PPU's I/O latch**, as any write to `$2004` does. After a DMA, `$2002`'s low five bits read the last byte transferred. The MiSTer core already behaved this way.
- **KS7032 (mapper 142)** now shows PRG-ROM at `$6000`, as its NESdev page documents. Before, it read a work RAM full of zeroes there.

## Measured and closed

- **The MMC3 M2-edge filter lever**, which ADR 0002 left for a maintainer decision, was tried and **refuted**. Filter thresholds 2, 3 and 4 produce identical MMC3 results. The shortest low time at any IRQ-clocking A12 rise is 91 CPU cycles on the ROMs it was meant to fix, so no threshold from 1 to 39 changes a single clock.
- **T-ORACLE-001**, the MMC3 IRQ that fires late, is not caused by where the A12 rise lands. The rise is at dot 260, exactly the dot the NESdev MMC3 page names, and the residual stands.
- **AccuracyCoin `APU Register Activation`** reports code 2 because the OAM-DMA bus conflict clocked the controller port. The ROM treats both outcomes as success; consoles differ here.
- **VRC7 rhythm mode** has nothing to implement: VRC7 has no rhythm DAC. A test pins that writing `$0E` changes no output.
- **The PPU write-placement residual** was re-measured. Moving writes to phi2 loses 2 to 6 AccuracyCoin entries and gains none, so the placement stays as shipped.
- **`.fm2` Four Score P3/P4 import** moves to v3.0.0. It needs a public struct to grow two fields, which is a breaking change.

## Test coverage

**49 committed test ROMs that no test ran are now gated.** Each is checked by the strongest verdict it supports:

- 13 report a real pass through blargg's `$6000` protocol;
- 23 Holy Mapperel variants each report the detail code `0000`;
- one data-report ROM is pinned;
- 12 visual or audio ROMs are pinned by hash. These are regression pins, not accuracy verdicts.

## The MiSTer core

The RTL is unchanged, so the bitstreams attached here are **v2.9.2's files, byte for byte**:

- on-die md5 `c17b0f37d5c49b150c023734b583f468`;
- off-die md5 `75ae3a99e840e29675ded9898dae127d`.

Its co-simulation ladder gained coverage and lost two blind spots:

- **The PPU I/O-latch decay groups have a stimulus.** A new ROM refreshes the low bits of the latch once, then only ever reads `$2002`. The three decay mutations every earlier ROM left inert are now caught.
- **The read-modify-write double write is covered.** Both of its mutations are caught by the per-cycle bus gate built around read-modify-write.
- **Two boot goldens were four cycles short** of the window the core runs, so its last four records went unchecked. Both are re-cut, and a new CI audit keeps the two windows equal.

- **Six of 77 checkpoint streams are not compared**, where the README said none were. Two are documented exclusions. The other four belong to AccuracyCoin sub-test ROMs gated by their verdict byte, because the latch difference fixed above dominated their streams; they are registered when the pinned oracle moves.

The oracle changes above reach the MiSTer core when its pinned oracle moves, at v2.9.9. The RTL they need lands there, under that release's seed sweep.

**No hardware has run any bitstream.**

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo test --workspace --features test-roms` | 2,905 passed, 0 failed, 20 ignored |
| AccuracyCoin / nestest | 144/144 / 0-diff |
| fmt, clippy (every feature set, all three wasm builds), rustdoc, no_std build | clean |
| MiSTer co-simulation ladder | on-die **174 passed, 0 failed, 1 expected failure**, off-die (`USE_SDRAM=1`) **175 passed, 0 failed, 1 expected failure**; each one frozen-worktree run, nothing skipped |

## Install

- Download the pre-built binaries for Linux, macOS, and Windows below.
- The MiSTer core bitstreams are attached below: `RustyNES_MiSTer-v2.9.5.rbf` (on-die, also as `RustyNES_20260928.rbf`) and `RustyNES_MiSTer-v2.9.5-offdie.rbf`. They are v2.9.2's files, so the MiSTer menu shows build date 260928. Neither has run on hardware.
- The WebAssembly build is live at [doublegate.github.io/RustyNES](https://doublegate.github.io/RustyNES/).
- The RetroArch core is in RetroArch's Online Updater on the platforms the libretro buildbot publishes to.
